mappings.note: Election against inheritance as the route to executive power. Comparative government under the goal.
The Lichchhavis within the Vajji mahajanapada, cited as an early republican tradition. The chapter uses it as an ancestor of democratic practice, so the civics goal.
Accountability to the electorate as a core principle of democracy. The working of democracy under the goal.

A citizen whose right to equality is infringed by a policy working out what recourse the courts give - interpreting a real issue with reference to the right to equality, which is LO-177's wording. Not the bare goal, because the right to equality is the substance.
Kautilya's threefold duties of internal administration, cited for what governments are for. The purpose-of-government framing keeps it in the civics goal.
Names one essential function of government. Functions of government under the goal.
India's form of government. Institutions of Indian democracy, so the goal.
The literal meaning of democracy. The chapter's founding concept under the goal.
The people as the ultimate source of authority in a democracy. The goal's own subject.
Names the legislative function. An organ of government under the goal.
Names the executive function. Same lane as its two sibling items on the organs of government.
Names the judicial function. Completes the set of three organs under the goal.
Attributes the famous definition of democracy to Lincoln. A recall about the concept, so the goal.
Names the constitution as the book of fundamental rules. Constitutional values under the goal.
Names the principle that everyone is to be treated equally in a democracy. This is the equality outcome stated directly.
Names universal adult franchise as the principle giving every adult a vote. Political equality, in line with the other franchise items.
The judiciary as the organ protecting fundamental rights. An institution of democracy, so the goal rather than the equality outcome.
Switzerland as the country where women got the vote only in 1971. A fact about how late equal suffrage arrived, so the equality outcome.
Names direct democracy. A form of democracy under the goal.
Names representative democracy as the common form. Same lane as the direct-democracy item.
Explains accountability in a democracy. The working of democracy under the goal.
Names the Rajya Sabha as Parliament's other house. An institution of Indian democracy.
Analyses how the absence of democratic principles shapes daily life and awareness in North Korea. A judgement about government types, so the goal.
Long-term consequences for a society under a dictator. Comparative government under the goal.
Separation of powers as the guard against abuse of power. A constitutional principle under the goal.

Reads a comparison table in which universal franchise, equality among citizens and freedom of speech belong only to democracy, to explain why it serves everyone's wellbeing. Equality is the axis of the table, so LO-175.
Challenges in moving from monarchy or colonial rule to stable democracy, with India as the case. The working of Indian democracy, so the goal.
Vigilant citizens as the safeguard of democracy, set against its hurdles. A judgement about how democracy is sustained.
The limitation of direct democracy in large countries. Comparative government under the goal.
How representative governments are held to account. The working of democracy, so the goal.
The executive's relation to the legislature in parliamentary and presidential systems. Comparative government.
Explains separation of powers across the three organs. A constitutional principle under the goal.
How the Lichchhavis practised republican principles. Early democratic practice, which the chapter treats as background to Indian democracy.
What the Uttaramerur inscriptions reveal about Chola village self-government. Democratic process at the local level, which the goal names explicitly.
The limits on who counted as a citizen in the Greek republics - exclusion from participation. The item turns on unequal political rights, so the equality outcome rather than the general goal.
Explains rajadharma as the duty binding an ancient king. The chapter's early standard for accountable rule, so the civics goal.
Absolute against constitutional monarchy with examples. Comparative government under the goal.
The defining feature of a theocracy. Comparative government.
Conditions in North Korea from Shane's story. Life under a non-democratic regime, so the comparative-government goal.
